summary:
A magnitude-7.1 earthquake struck Japan's Kyushu island today, shaking the region with the highest intensity on the Japanese scale and triggering tsunami warnings for waves up to 1 meter. Residents along the coast have been urged to evacuate immediately. No casualties have been reported so far, but officials are bracing for potential damage aftershocks. The quake comes as Japan remains on high alert for seismic activity.

In Washington, two key meetings are set to take place this week. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu meets President Trump for the first time since US-Israeli strikes on Iran strained relations. Both leaders are expected to downplay public friction over ceasefire negotiations. Separately, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky will also visit the White House, seeking stronger air defense cooperation. Trump has reportedly been impressed by Ukraine's recent battlefield gains, signaling a possible shift in ties.

Mediators are working on a quick fix to reopen the Strait of Hormuz during a lull in fighting between Iran and its adversaries. Iran and Oman are seeking an agreement to resume shipping, which could pave the way for broader peace talks. Iran denies direct negotiations with the US. Meanwhile, Uganda has launched emergency food relief after at least 19 deaths from hunger were reported in the drought-stricken Karamoja region. The area's 1.5 million people face acute food shortages and malnutrition.

Across Asia, extreme rainfall has triggered flash floods and typhoons from Afghanistan to Taiwan. In eastern Afghanistan, homes built of stone and mud have collapsed, and crops have been washed away. Residents say the rains are coming heavier and earlier each year, a pattern scientists link to climate breakdown. The destruction is widespread, with tens of thousands affected across the continent.
